title: The Cairo Lab That Chose an Accreditation Egypt Did Not Require
conflicts: Slate error: Dr Moamena Kamel did not found Al Borg (founded 1990 by four doctors, per IDH and its 2015 prospectus); she founded MK Lab in 1979, which merged with Al Mokhtabar in 2004, and IDH (formed around Al Borg by Abraaj in 2008) bought Al Mokhtabar in 2012. Kamel's field: 'professor of immunology' (IDH, prospectus, IFC, Lionesses) vs 'a pathologist' (her daughter, CAP 2021); both given, attributed. El Sherbini joined in 2001 (Lionesses) vs 2004 (CAP; prospectus has her managing director from 2004); story uses 'in 2001 by one of her accounts' and running Al Mokhtabar by 2007. Accreditation continuity: El Sherbini claimed 'ten straight years' of CAP accreditation in 2021, but the 2015 prospectus says it expired in April 2014 when unrest delayed CAP's inspection and IDH announced the new Mega Lab's certification in February 2018; story follows the filings. CAP says Kamel founded 'Al Mokhtabar' in 1979; IDH says MK Lab. Branch and test counts vary widely by entity and year; none used.
notes: Episode changed from the 1979 founding (documented only in a line or two; no interview with Dr Kamel found in English or Arabic) to her daughter Hend El Sherbini's documented 2007 decision to seek CAP accreditation, told mainly in El Sherbini's own words in a 2021 CAP interview, with the 1979 founding, Kamel's 1998 ISO 9001 and the 2014 lapse as context. Founder field names both women. Company given as 'Al Mokhtabar (Integrated Diagnostics Holdings from 2012)'. ISO 9001 is called certification, not accreditation. Funding 'bootstrapped' because Al Mokhtabar was family-owned until 2012 (a 2007 MOU to sell 49 per cent to Al Muhaidib was never completed). talQen mentioned once, in the reflection. Quote stance: affirms.
